notes: Pass 1: All three www.clio.com pages requested (pricing, home, integrations) returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare challenge page (title Just a moment..., 16 characters of text). robots.txt allows these paths. Per protocol there was no retry; further www.clio.com pages (about, press, security, product) were not requested because the host challenged every request, so all 83 claims are unverifiable and no cause tracing applies. help.clio.com (cited once) was not read: it is a data-migration article that would settle none of the claims. page-candidates.json lists americanbar.org as Clio's home page, which is a data error. Not coded because they are outside the 13 types: integration counts (200+, 250+, 300+, hundreds), a US$5 billion valuation, the year Clio Duo launched (2025, three Claude answers), payout timing, and Business Associate Agreements. One answer (q8 Claude run 1) says Rocket Matter integrates with Clio; it was treated as a statement about another vendor and not coded. Hedged tier statements (may require, can depend on, not all included) were not coded, except where they name Clio Grow and a plan or add-on route (C40). Answers disagree with each other on plan names (Starter, Core, Signature, Elite versus EasyStart, Essentials, Advanced, Complete), entry price ($39, $49, about $59) and top-tier price ($129+, $139, $149); a readable pricing page would be needed to class any of them. Pass 2 (8 Oct): the pricing, home and integrations pages were each read once in a real browser, and the about page (https://www.clio.com/about/) once in a browser; every claim was re-classed against those snapshots. Now true: C01, C04, C14, C16, C20 to C23, C39, C40, C45, C49, C50, C60, C62, C67, C78 and C83. Now wrong: C15 (a Starting Price cell of Custom against the published starting price). All other pass 1 claims stay unverifiable. Added under the 8 Oct clarification (integration counts and BAAs are in scope): C84 to C87 (250+, over 200, 300+ and hundreds of integrations, all true: the integrations page gives 250+ and the home and about pages 300+), C88 (mobile use, unverifiable), C89 (BAAs, unverifiable), C90 (the PI Essentials name, split from C45 because the add-on is on the page and the name is not; unverifiable) and C91 (per-user monthly basis, true); new instances on C02 (q3 Claude run 1, a Pricing line under the Clio heading) and C63 (q7 Claude run 1). Judgement calls for review: (1) the pricing snapshot prints Starting at $49/user with no billing period; C01, C04 and C91 are true on price and per-user basis, while the $39 and about $59 entry prices (C02, C03, C08) stay unverifiable because two of the $39 answers tie it to annual billing and the page does not say which term $49 is. (2) The page lists Starter, Core, Signature and Elite; EasyStart, Essentials, Advanced and Complete (C24 to C27) and their prices stay unverifiable because absence from the list is not an explicit contradiction and no page dates a rename. (3) C48 (free plan) stays unverifiable: the pages offer a 7-day free trial and only priced or on-request plans on the practice management tab, but none states there is no free plan, and the Legal work and Platform tabs were not captured. (4) C16 (transparent tiered pricing) is true on tiers and an advertised entry price; only Starter carries a price. (5) C78 and C83 rest on an article title listed on the integrations page. (6) C63 (cloud-based) stays unverifiable: no page read says so. Cause for C15: of the ten pages the answer cites, the 8am MyCase blog, Taqtics and Quickbase pages (already read in this study for other vendors) and the Stack Compare, Pagelightprime, MyLegalAcademy and PracticePanther comparison pages (read now) do not carry it; research.com and Capterra answered HTTP 403 when read for other vendors, and clio.com/compare was not requested because that host challenged every plain fetch; cause not found. Not coded: lines that state Clio tier gating only in contrast to MyCase or CosmoLex (q4 Claude runs 1 to 3 on AI, texting and eSignature; q4 Google AI Mode run 2 on accounting), and q2 Claude run 2 (All three top platforms offer free trials), which does not name the three.
